description: Preview how often an alert would fire BEFORE creating it. Sweeps the past N days (default 7, max 30) for the given entity (or keyword, for kind=KEYWORD_MENTION) and returns the total match count, a per-day breakdown, and a small sample of the most recent matches with episode context. Use this to size an alert (REALTIME vs DAILY vs WEEKLY cadence) or to confirm the entity slug watches the right thing, then call particle_alert_create with the same entity slug (for KEYWORD_MENTION, the same keyword instead). Pass the same `filters` you plan to save so the estimate matches what the alert would surface — the languages and speaker_roles axes narrow the sweep; relevance and source_popularity are read-time projections that don't, so the count is an upper bound when relevance=RELEVANT. Starts a background sweep and caches its progress and results; it does not create an alert or send notifications.

entities.description: The entity to preview, as a single slug (from the resolve tools), same as particle_alert_create.entities — exactly one for entity kinds, omitted for KEYWORD_MENTION.

filters.description: Same as particle_alert_create.filters. Pass the filters you intend to save so the estimate reflects what the alert would actually surface. languages, speaker_roles, source_popularity and speaker_statement_characteristics narrow the historical sweep exactly as they narrow new matches; relevance is graded only on new matches, so setting it leaves the count unchanged (the estimate is an upper bound when relevance=RELEVANT).

languages.description: Primary language tags the source episode must be in: a 2-3 letter primary tag (e.g. 'en', 'de', 'sma'). A region or script subtag (e.g. 'pt-BR', 'zh-Hant') is accepted for readability but matching is on the PRIMARY tag only — 'pt-BR' surfaces every Portuguese episode regardless of region, and 'pt-BR' + 'pt-PT' collapse to one. Empty or missing means all languages are surfaced. Case-insensitive; echoed in canonical primary-tag form.

relevance.description: EVERYTHING (default) returns both on-target and incidental matches — the watched entity is correctly identified in both, only the depth of discussion differs. RELEVANT narrows to on-target only: matches where the watched entity is the subject being discussed, dropping passing mentions. Wrong-entity matches (name collisions) are globally suppressed before any filter runs.

source_popularity.description: ANY (default) keeps matches from every source. POPULAR keeps only matches whose source podcast scores in the top 5% by chart-popularity percentile (Podcast.Popularity >= 0.95; cume_dist over current chart entries, multi-region weighted). Podcasts that aren't currently charting drop out.

speaker_roles.description: PODCAST_SPEAKER alerts only — sending this on an ENTITY_MENTION alert returns an unprocessable_entity error. REPLACES (not intersects with) the default appearance set. Default when omitted is GUEST, PANELIST, CORRESPONDENT, AUDIENCE, SOUNDBITE_SPEAKER — HOST is excluded because hosting the show isn't an appearance. Setting ['HOST'] flips that; setting ['GUEST'] alone narrows further. Input casing is not significant — 'guest' and 'GUEST' are the same value — and the filter is stored and returned in canonical uppercase form. Raw STT/LLM labels like CALLER or REPORTER are not accepted.

speaker_statement_characteristics.description: ENTITY_MENTION alerts only — sending it on a PODCAST_SPEAKER or KEYWORD_MENTION alert returns unprocessable_entity. Keeps a match only when one of its mention lines was said the way you ask, the same filter particle_podcast_find_mentions takes: {'sentiment': ['negative']} for criticism of the watched entity, {'specificity': ['specific'], 'temporal_orientation': ['future']} for concrete predictions about it, {'certainty': ['confident']} for confident claims. Labels on one axis OR together, axes AND. Mention lines the filter does not accept are not marked as mentions and do not count. Put how something is said here, never in the alert's title or keyword.

certainty.description: How sure the speaker sounds. 'confident' for flat assertions and high conviction; 'hedged' for maybe, I think, it could, and other hedging; 'neutral' for neither.

sentiment.description: The statement's tone. 'positive' for optimistic, bullish, approving or praising lines; 'negative' for skeptical, bearish, critical or worried ones; 'neutral' for lines that clearly lean neither way.

specificity.description: Whether the line commits to something concrete. 'specific' for names, numbers, dates and mechanisms (concrete claims); 'vague' for generalities; 'neutral' for neither.

temporal_orientation.description: Where the line points in time. 'future' for predictions, forecasts, plans and expectations; 'past' for looking back; 'present' for how things are now.

keyword.description: Same as particle_alert_create.keyword — required for KEYWORD_MENTION. A phrase that matched more than 700 podcast episodes in the past week is rejected as too broad, as on create.

kind.description: Signal to preview. Defaults to ENTITY_MENTION.

output_format.description: Output serialization. 'markdown' (default) returns the LLM-facing rendering. 'json' returns the structured payload as JSON text — use only for programmatic chaining where exact field extraction matters; the JSON shape is larger and noisier for an LLM to read.

window_days.description: How many days back to sweep (1-30, default 7).
